name: MXNB
oneLiner: MXNB is Juno/Bitso's MXN-pegged stablecoin backed 1:1 by peso reserves at regulated banks with quarterly attestations; now issued from El Salvador under CNAD.
collateral: Mexican peso (MXN) fiat reserves and cash-equivalent assets held across multiple regulated financial institutions; beginning April 8, 2026, MXNB is issued by Nvio Pagos El Salvador, S.A. de C.V., an authorised digital-asset issuer in El Salvador
pegMechanism: 1:1 MXN fiat-collateralized stablecoin; Juno/MXNB materials describe reserve parity, token burn/redemption through issuer rails, and quarterly third-party attestations confirming reserves exceed circulating supply

blacklistabilityReview.evidence: Explicit Yes retained: centralized governance metadata indicates issuer or admin control; registry links were reviewed for direct freeze, blacklist, pause, burn, or upgrade authority.

reserves.name: MXN fiat reserves and cash-equivalents at Mexican financial institutions

mintAuthority.summary: MXNB is issued by Juno/Bitso (now Nvio Pagos El Salvador under CNAD) against 1:1 MXN reserves; the token is a Circle FiatToken-style proxy where a masterMinter controls minter allowances, so supply is created by issuer-controlled minter roles.

controls.label: MXNB masterMinter / issuer minter roles (Nvio/Bitso)
controls.evidence: MXNB is forked from Circle's FiatToken contracts: a masterMinter address configures the set of minters and per-minter mint allowances, behind an upgradeable proxy; the issuer (Juno/Bitso, now Nvio Pagos El Salvador under CNAD) holds these privileged roles.

review.evidence: MXNB's published architecture is a Circle FiatToken fork using a masterMinter/minter allowance model behind a proxy upgrade pattern; mint and redeem are issuer-managed against 1:1 MXN reserves with quarterly attestations, with issuance authority held by Juno/Bitso and reassigned to Nvio Pagos El Salvador (CNAD-authorized). Live masterMinter/proxy admin addresses not independently read.
unresolvedQuestions: Resolve the live masterMinter, minter, and proxy-admin addresses (and whether they are now Nvio-controlled) before raising confidence.
